name.text: Reducible equations: quadratic in sin θ or cos θ (0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°)

questiontext.text:
Solve the equation

\[ {@eqn@} \qquad\text{for } 0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ. \]

Type a list of values like [30, 150], in any order; decimals are accepted in parts (b) and (c). Give angles in degrees.

(a) Let \(x = [[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]]\theta\). The equation becomes \({@pexp@} = 0\). Factorise the left-hand side fully.

\({@pexp@} = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prta]]

(b) Hence find the values of \(x\).

\(x = \) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prtb]]

(c) Hence find all the values of \(\theta\) for \(0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ\).

\(\theta = \) [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prtc]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

This is a reducible equation: it is a quadratic equation in \([[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]]\theta\). We replace \([[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]]\theta\) by \(x\), solve the quadratic, then solve each simple trigonometric equation.

(a) Factorising

Step 1: substitute. With \(x = [[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]]\theta\), the equation \({@eqn@}\) becomes \({@pexp@} = 0\).

Step 2: factorise. [[if test="is(r1=0)"]]There is no constant term, so take out the common factor \(x\)[[else]]Find two factors whose product gives the quadratic, and check by expanding[[/if]]:

\[ {@pexp@} = {@pfac@}. \]

(b) Values of \(x\)

Step 3: set each factor equal to zero. \({@f1@} = 0\) gives \(x = {@r1@}\), and \({@f2@} = 0\) gives \(x = {@r2@}\). So \(x = {@rts@}\).

(c) Values of \(\theta\)

Step 4: solve each equation for \(\theta\).

  • [[if test="is(fs=1 and r1=0)"]]\(\sin\theta = {@r1@}\): the point on the unit circle is on the \(x\)-axis, so \(\theta = 0^\circ,\ 180^\circ,\ 360^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=1 and r1=1/2)"]]\(\sin\theta = {@r1@}\): the reference angle is \(\alpha = 30^\circ\). Sine is positive in Quadrants I and II, so \(\theta = 30^\circ\) and \(\theta = 180^\circ - 30^\circ = 150^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=1 and r1=-1/2)"]]\(\sin\theta = {@r1@}\): the reference angle is \(\alpha = 30^\circ\). Sine is negative in Quadrants III and IV, so \(\theta = 180^\circ + 30^\circ = 210^\circ\) and \(\theta = 360^\circ - 30^\circ = 330^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=1 and r1=1)"]]\(\sin\theta = {@r1@}\): the point is at the top of the unit circle, so \(\theta = 90^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=1 and r1=-1)"]]\(\sin\theta = {@r1@}\): the point is at the bottom of the unit circle, so \(\theta = 270^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=1 and abs(r1)>1)"]]\(\sin\theta = {@r1@}\): no solution, because \(-1 \le \sin\theta \le 1\) for every angle. This value is rejected.[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=2 and r1=0)"]]\(\cos\theta = {@r1@}\): the point on the unit circle is on the \(y\)-axis, so \(\theta = 90^\circ,\ 270^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=2 and r1=1/2)"]]\(\cos\theta = {@r1@}\): the reference angle is \(\alpha = 60^\circ\). Cosine is positive in Quadrants I and IV, so \(\theta = 60^\circ\) and \(\theta = 360^\circ - 60^\circ = 300^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=2 and r1=-1/2)"]]\(\cos\theta = {@r1@}\): the reference angle is \(\alpha = 60^\circ\). Cosine is negative in Quadrants II and III, so \(\theta = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ\) and \(\theta = 180^\circ + 60^\circ = 240^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=2 and r1=1)"]]\(\cos\theta = {@r1@}\): the point is at the right-hand end of the unit circle, so \(\theta = 0^\circ\) and \(\theta = 360^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=2 and r1=-1)"]]\(\cos\theta = {@r1@}\): the point is at the left-hand end of the unit circle, so \(\theta = 180^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=2 and abs(r1)>1)"]]\(\cos\theta = {@r1@}\): no solution, because \(-1 \le \cos\theta \le 1\) for every angle. This value is rejected.[[/if]]
  • [[if test="is(fs=1 and r2=0)"]]\(\sin\theta = {@r2@}\): the point on the unit circle is on the \(x\)-axis, so \(\theta = 0^\circ,\ 180^\circ,\ 360^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=1 and r2=1/2)"]]\(\sin\theta = {@r2@}\): the reference angle is \(\alpha = 30^\circ\). Sine is positive in Quadrants I and II, so \(\theta = 30^\circ\) and \(\theta = 180^\circ - 30^\circ = 150^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=1 and r2=-1/2)"]]\(\sin\theta = {@r2@}\): the reference angle is \(\alpha = 30^\circ\). Sine is negative in Quadrants III and IV, so \(\theta = 180^\circ + 30^\circ = 210^\circ\) and \(\theta = 360^\circ - 30^\circ = 330^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=1 and r2=1)"]]\(\sin\theta = {@r2@}\): the point is at the top of the unit circle, so \(\theta = 90^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=1 and r2=-1)"]]\(\sin\theta = {@r2@}\): the point is at the bottom of the unit circle, so \(\theta = 270^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=1 and abs(r2)>1)"]]\(\sin\theta = {@r2@}\): no solution, because \(-1 \le \sin\theta \le 1\) for every angle. This value is rejected.[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=2 and r2=0)"]]\(\cos\theta = {@r2@}\): the point on the unit circle is on the \(y\)-axis, so \(\theta = 90^\circ,\ 270^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=2 and r2=1/2)"]]\(\cos\theta = {@r2@}\): the reference angle is \(\alpha = 60^\circ\). Cosine is positive in Quadrants I and IV, so \(\theta = 60^\circ\) and \(\theta = 360^\circ - 60^\circ = 300^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=2 and r2=-1/2)"]]\(\cos\theta = {@r2@}\): the reference angle is \(\alpha = 60^\circ\). Cosine is negative in Quadrants II and III, so \(\theta = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ\) and \(\theta = 180^\circ + 60^\circ = 240^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=2 and r2=1)"]]\(\cos\theta = {@r2@}\): the point is at the right-hand end of the unit circle, so \(\theta = 0^\circ\) and \(\theta = 360^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=2 and r2=-1)"]]\(\cos\theta = {@r2@}\): the point is at the left-hand end of the unit circle, so \(\theta = 180^\circ\).[[/if]][[if test="is(fs=2 and abs(r2)>1)"]]\(\cos\theta = {@r2@}\): no solution, because \(-1 \le \cos\theta \le 1\) for every angle. This value is rejected.[[/if]]

Step 5: combine the solutions. Collect the angles from [[if test="is(nval=2)"]]both equations[[else]]the equation that has solutions[[/if]], remembering that the range includes both \(0^\circ\) and \(360^\circ\):

\[ \theta = {@sall@}. \]

The graph of \(y = [[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]]\theta\) shows each solution as a point where the curve meets one of the lines \(y = {@r1@}\) or \(y = {@r2@}\).[[if test="is(nval=1)"]] The line \(y = {@r2@}\) never meets the curve, because the curve stays between \(-1\) and \(1\).[[/if]]

questiondescription.text: Objective: solve reducible trigonometric equations (Type 2) that are quadratic in sin θ or cos θ, by substitution, factorising, rejecting values outside −1 to 1, and solving for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°.

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

falsefeedback.text: Your expression does not expand to \({@pexp@}\). Multiply out your brackets to check your factors.

Your expression is equal to the quadratic, but it is not written as a product of factors. [[if test="is(r1=0)"]]Look for a common factor.[[else]]Find two brackets that multiply to give the quadratic.[[/if]]

truefeedback.text: Check the signs. If a factor equals zero, solve it for \(x\): for example, \(2x - 1 = 0\) gives \(x = \tfrac{1}{2}\), not \(-\tfrac{1}{2}\).

falsefeedback.text: Set each factor from part (a) equal to zero and solve for \(x\).

truefeedback.text: Nearly there. The range \(0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ\) includes both end points. Check whether \(0^\circ\) or \(360^\circ\) is also a solution.

node.description: Solved only one of the two equations

truefeedback.text: Those are the solutions of only one of the equations. Each value of \(x\) from part (b) gives its own equation in \(\theta\); solve both and combine the answers.

node.description: Solved with the signs of x reversed

truefeedback.text: Those angles solve the equations with the opposite signs. Use your values of \(x\) from part (b) and the CAST rule to choose the right quadrants.

falsefeedback.text: Solve \([[if test="is(fs=1)"]]\sin[[else]]\cos[[/if]]\theta = x\) for each value of \(x\) from part (b). Reject any value that is less than \(-1\) or greater than \(1\), and list every angle from \(0^\circ\) to \(360^\circ\).
